sections.h2: Rockwall County Clerk's property records office
sections.html:
Deeds, deeds of trust, lien filings and plats for Rockwall County go through the Clerk's Property Department at Suite 100, 1111 E Yellowjacket Lane, Rockwall, TX 75087. Most GPS and internet maps put the building in the wrong spot. It sits about 0.3 miles east of Goliad and SH 205.

  • Phone: 972-204-6300. Fax: 972-204-6309.
  • Open weekdays from 8 a.m. until 5 p.m., closed on county holidays.
  • Cutoff: final transactions should be finished by 4 p.m.
  • ID: since House Bill 1195, a valid ID is required for any document presented in person.

The Official Public Records can be searched online, and copies and eCertified copies can be bought there. Paper certified copies are mailed by the clerk's office. A buyer who picks the In Person option can fill a cart online but pays at the counter.

Treat the online search as a starting point. House Bill 4350, effective June 20, 2025, requires some information to be redacted from certain instruments, so a screen may show a record that is incomplete or altered. Title examiners work from the official records at the clerk's office.

Plan on $25 for page one and $4 for each page after it. Senate Bill 1612 repealed the old $1 filing fee under Local Government Code Section 291.008(d) from January 1, 2024.

Rockwall County Clerk property records filing fees
Document or serviceFee
First page of a document$25
Each additional page$4
Each page of a plat$49
Each grantor or grantee above five names$0.25
UCC financing statement, 1 or 2 pages$35
UCC financing statement, more than 2 pages$50

Plats also need tax certificates, which are filed at their regular price. The clerk cannot refund an overpayment made by check, so call the office to confirm what applies to your instrument before you send it.

sections.h2: Formatting rules that get filings rejected
sections.html:
Paperwork gets turned away over format more often than you would expect. The county's general requirements include:

  • Leave a 2-inch by 4-inch area empty at the foot of the final page for the certification label. If the area is crowded the label goes on the back, which adds a page and a $4 charge. E-filed documents follow the same rule.
  • Signatures must be originals or certified copies, since the clerk cannot file copies.
  • Print or type each name below its signature line.
  • An abstract of judgment that omits the plaintiff's address costs double to file.
  • A correction instrument has to conform to Texas Property Code Chapter 5.

Plats face a longer checklist. Sheet size runs from 18 by 24 inches up to 24 by 36. The clerk wants a single black-line copy with the original seals and signatures, a full legal description, notarized signatures and a surveyor's certification. Inside a city's extraterritorial jurisdiction the city must approve it. Original tax certificates from every taxing unit, dated within 90 days of filing and showing no delinquent tax, must come with it.

sections.h2: What must a deed show before the clerk accepts it?
sections.html:
Under Property Code Section 12.001(b), the clerk can record a real property conveyance only when it carries a signature plus an acknowledgment or sworn statement before a notary or similar officer, or two subscribing witnesses. County clerks serve as recorders, and filing happens in the county where the land is located.

Estate paperwork lands here too. For a muniment of title, the court order and will are lodged with the clerk in the property's county. A transfer on death deed has to be on record before the owner's death. The small estate affidavit suits an intestate estate worth $75,000 or less excluding the homestead, and a homestead copy is recorded with the clerk. An affidavit of heirship is only a sworn statement that no court has checked, and nothing obliges a buyer or lender to rely on it.

A seller with a gap in the title should pull the chain of records early. A missing heir, an unreleased lien or an unrecorded deed will surface at the title company, and the cure usually means a fresh filing in this office.

sections.h2: Foreclosure notices and mechanic's lien bonds
sections.html:
Foreclosure notices are posted on the county's site. Trustee sales happen on the first Tuesday of each month outside on the courthouse steps at 1111 Yellowjacket Lane. The notice of sale is filed with the clerk and posted at the courthouse door at least 21 days beforehand, and the auction takes place between 10 a.m. and 4 p.m. After a notice of default, the borrower has 20 days to reinstate by paying what is past due.

Mechanic's liens have an exit in this office. Under Property Code Sections 53.171 to 53.174, anyone may file a bond to indemnify against a lien. The lien is discharged once a compliant bond is filed, notice goes to each claimant by certified mail, and the bond and notice are recorded. The bond must generally be double the lien amount, or when the claims top $40,000, the larger of 1.5 times the liens or $40,000 plus the liens. The clerk charges the usual $25 and $4 page fees, plus $1 a page for copies and the mailing postage.

A free service called Property Fraud Alert sends a phone or email warning when a document is recorded under your name. One phone number can enroll 3 names and one email address can enroll 4.

sections.h2: Who handles Rockwall County values and tax bills?
sections.html:
Values come from the Rockwall Central Appraisal District, 841 Justin Rd., Rockwall, 972-771-2034. The county tax office is at 101 E. Rusk St., Ste. 101, phone 972-204-6130, but it does not collect property tax. The appraisal district may collect, so call it to learn where to pay.

Active units include Rockwall ISD and Royse City ISD, the cities of Rockwall, Fate, Royse City, Heath and McLendon-Chisholm, and parts of Wylie, Rowlett, Dallas and Garland. Seven municipal utility districts, three public improvement districts and the Club Municipal Management District #1 add more lines for some addresses.

Each year's tax lien takes hold on January 1 and the owner on that date answers for the bill. Liens for state taxes are entered by the clerk in the state tax lien book. For city permits or code questions, call the municipality if the property lies inside city limits. Outside city limits, the county's Development Services department covers the county engineer, GIS and 911 addressing, environmental health, fire marshal, and road and bridge.

A sale ends at the clerk's counter or inbox. Before listing, get a copy of your vesting deed and any recorded liens from the Official Public Records, then compare them with what your title company finds. If something is missing, such as a lien release or a deed from an earlier owner, fix it before you accept an offer so the closing does not stall.

The deed must be signed and acknowledged, and it must be filed in the county where the land sits. Allow time to arrive before 4 p.m. if you file in person, bring a valid ID, and leave the empty area at the foot of the last page. Ask about the filing fee before you send a check, since an overpayment cannot be refunded.

faqs.q: Where can I file a deed in Rockwall County?
faqs.a: At the County Clerk's Property Department, 1111 E Yellowjacket Lane, Suite 100, Rockwall, TX 75087. Bring a valid ID, since one is required for in-person filings, and plan to finish by 4 p.m.

faqs.q: What will the Rockwall County Clerk charge for a deed?
faqs.a: The fee is $25 for page one and $4 for every page after it, plus $0.25 for each grantor or grantee past five. A last page without the empty label area also costs an extra $4.

faqs.q: Can I search Rockwall County property records online?
faqs.a: Yes, the Official Public Records have an online search where copies are for sale. Some information is redacted there, so go to the clerk's office for certified records.

faqs.q: When are Rockwall County foreclosure sales held?
faqs.a: On the first Tuesday of every month, at the front steps of the Rockwall County Courthouse. Questions go to the trustee named on a notice.

faqs.q: Does the Rockwall County tax office collect property tax?
faqs.a: No. The appraisal district may collect instead, so call the Rockwall Central Appraisal District at 972-771-2034 to learn where your bill is paid.
